## Hypothesis history

- after step 12: DNA replication 0.62, Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.23, DNA damage 0.10, Microtubule destabilizers 0.03, Actin disruptors 0.03

## Conclusion

Why: All 4 wells show large cells/nuclei with intact tubulin/actin; NSC 4/4 for DNA replication.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Pulse-label with EdU/BrdU plus DNA-content flow cytometry to test S-phase synthesis inhibition and cell-cycle arrest, and stain for DNA-break markers to separate replication stress from damage.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Protocol NSC is unanimous (4/4) across four doses (1, 3, 10, 30 µM, indices 3-6) and independent of dose, with summed similarity 1.45 concentrated entirely in DNA replication; the k=10 atlas neighbours are 6 DNA replication / 3 Aurora kinase inhibitors / 1 DNA damage, so the top class leads the runner-up on the pre-specified primary readout, not on a single well. The quantitative morphology supports a DNA-content / S-phase-class effect and discriminates against the runner-up: cell_area z +9.8 to +23.5 and nuc_area z +3.9 to +7.0 at every dose, while frac_multinucleate_proxy is at or below DMSO (z −3.8, 0.1, −4.9, −0.9) and tubulin/actin features are near zero, arguing against failed-cytokinesis/binucleation as the driver. I have weighed the main caveats: per-well NSC similarity is only modest absolute (0.34–0.38), the microscopist report (e5) names Aurora kinase inhibitors, the 1 µM frac_mitotic_like spike (z +10.4) is dose-inconsistent (z ≈ −0.9 to +0.2 elsewhere), and the sampled range is already saturated (dose-response rho −0.2/−0.8), so neither onset nor EC50 is pinned. Those caveats cap confidence, and the stated 0.62 is calibrated on the low side rather than over-claimed, leaving sensible residual mass on Aurora kinase inhibitors (0.23) and DNA damage (0.10). Budget is exhausted (4/4 used), and since the protocol call already agrees with the submitted conclusion and rests on four concordant doses with very large effect sizes, no affordable additional well or free analysis would plausibly overturn DNA replication.

## Unblinding

Compound: **floxuridine** (PubChem CID [5790](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5790))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: Thymidylate synthase inhibitor

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: the call was **DNA replication**, BBBC021 annotates **DNA replication**.

The final call is the nearest-neighbour vote over the 4 wells the agent chose (4/4). The Scientist's own call was **DNA replication** (agrees; right).

## Reflection

The DNA replication call was correct for floxuridine and rested on concordance across four independent acquisitions at 1, 3, 10 and 30 uM, each showing very large cell_area (z +9.8 to +23.5), large major axis and large-nucleus features, with NSC voting 4/4 for DNA replication. That consistency plus k-neighbour enrichment for DNA replication over Aurora kinase inhibitors and DNA damage justified favoring S-phase inhibition, which fits thymidylate synthase inhibition by fluorodeoxyuridine (PMID 1532343) and the reported intra-S checkpoint response to 5-fluorodeoxyuridine (PMID 38954736).

What limited confidence was absolute similarity only 0.34-0.38 per well, 3/10 neighbours as Aurora kinase inhibitors, and the microscopist report naming Aurora kinase inhibitors as candidate, so I kept residual probability on Aurora (0.23) and DNA damage (0.10) rather than over-claiming at 0.62. The dose-responses were already saturated with rho -0.20 for cell_area and rho -0.80 for nuc_area, and the 1 uM mitotic-like spike was dose-inconsistent, so neither onset nor EC50 was pinned.

Acquisition of mid/high doses first then bridging 1 and 10 uM was useful for showing phenotype continuity but used the 4-well budget without capturing a low-dose negative anchor; no affordable extra well would have overturned the unanimous vote, so the correct follow-up is a direct S-phase synthesis test rather than more morphology.

What was right:
- NSC 4/4 vote for DNA replication across 1, 3, 10 and 30 uM wells (e4, e9) with k-neighbours 6/10 DNA replication vs 3/10 Aurora and 1/10 DNA damage
- Persistent enlarged-cell / enlarged-nucleus signal: cell_area z +9.8 to +23.5, frac_large_nucleus z +17.5 and +14.6, cell_major_axis z +7.4 to +11.9 across e2, e3, e7, e8
- Down-weighting microtubule destabilizers and actin disruptors to 0.025 each and keeping Aurora/DNA damage as explicit alternatives instead of a single-class claim

What was wrong or missed:
- Microscopist visual check (e5) favored Aurora kinase inhibitors, which conflicted with NSC and reflected overlap between enlarged/polyploid-like morphology and mitotic failure phenotypes
- Per-well NSC similarities were modest in absolute terms (0.335-0.379) and the runner-up Aurora signal was non-trivial, so 0.62 confidence was appropriately capped rather than strong
- Dose-response acquisitions (e10, e11) were in a saturated range with non-significant rho -0.20 and -0.80, so they confirmed continuity but failed to define onset or EC50

Proposed next experiment: Pulse-label with EdU/BrdU plus DNA-content flow cytometry to test for S-phase synthesis inhibition and arrest, with parallel staining for DNA-break markers to separate replication stress from DNA damage.

## Citations

Citations verified: 3/3

- PMID [1532343](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/1532343/): Radiosensitization by fluorodeoxyuridine: effects of thymidylate synthase inhibition and cell synchronization. *Cancer Res* (1992) — Fluorodeoxyuridine acts via thymidylate synthase inhibition with effects on cell synchronization.
- PMID [38954736](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38954736/): REV3 promotes cellular tolerance to 5-fluorodeoxyuridine by activating translesion DNA synthesis and intra-S checkpoint. *PLoS Genet* (2024) — 5-fluorodeoxyuridine elicits intra-S checkpoint activation and translesion DNA synthesis tolerance via REV3.
- PMID [2947954](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2947954/): Comparison of the inhibitory effects of hydroxyurea, 5-fluorodeoxyuridine, 3,4-dihydroxybenzylamine, and methotrexate on human squamous cell carcinoma. *J Invest Dermatol* (1987) — 5-fluorodeoxyuridine inhibits proliferation in a comparison including hydroxyurea and methotrexate.
